evidence: Clear modular structure with 8 well-separated packages (bokeh, analyzer_tables, schemes, etc.) each with focused responsibilities
No external service interfaces or network calls indicating decoupled services; all functionality is within a single Python package
Use of shared utilities and internal imports (e.g., backtrader_plotting.utils used across modules) indicates tight integration
All demos and tests directly import and use core components (Bokeh, OptBrowser) without inter-service communication
Folder structure reflects domain decomposition (bokeh for visualization, analyzer_tables for result reporting, schemes for styling, live for streaming)
Shared data models and utilities (utils.py) used across modules without external APIs
No message queues, REST/gRPC endpoints, or container-based deployment signatures
risks: Risk of growing module coupling if new cross-cutting concerns are added without clear boundaries
Testing isolation may be challenging if modules are not explicitly designed for decoupling
Scaling options are limited to process-level (monolith), not service-level
